description: The conservative operating point selected from the tested k values based on the empirical safety-utilization trade-off.
wording_constraints: k=1.0 is NOT described as mathematically optimal, statistically optimal, globally optimal, or as having a textbook confidence interpretation.
It is the conservative operating point selected from the tested k values based on the empirical safety-utilization trade-off.

per_model_coverage_bucketed.k=1.0: Solar 93.9%, Load 88.4% — largest marginal gain from k=0.5 (+4.8pp solar, +9.3pp load)
per_model_coverage_bucketed.k=2.0: Solar 97.4%, Load 96.2% — high coverage, low utilization (70.1%)

evidence_summary.synthetic_decision_matrix_note: Evaluated on 176 synthetically aligned pairs (NOT real-world co-located). At k>=1.0, zero ALLOWs produced for BOTH 0.5 kW and 1.2 kW device powers. Only k=0.5 produces any ALLOWs (9 for 0.5 kW device: 8 correct, 1 incorrect; 0 for 1.2 kW). This demonstrates extreme conservatism in the synthetic setting.

1.2_kW.all_k: 0 ALLOWs for all k including k=0.5 — system never ALLOWs a 1.2 kW device in this synthetic pairing

rationale: k=1.0 is selected as the operating point based on: (1) the k 0.5->1.0 step produces the largest marginal coverage improvement (+4.8pp solar, +9.3pp load) relative to utilization cost (-6.3pp); (2) solar coverage 93.9% and load coverage 88.4% provide reasonable safety margins; (3) 81.5% solar utilization preserves usability; (4) the project safety-first principle prioritizes avoiding unsafe ALLOWs over maximizing utilization. The synthetic decision evaluation (176 pairs) cannot independently validate this choice because k>=1.0 produces zero ALLOWs — this reflects the structural conservatism of compounding solar and load safety margins in a small-scale synthetic pairing, not the real-world operating characteristics of the system.
extreme_conservatism_flag: At k>=1.0, the synthetic evaluation produces ZERO ALLOWs for BOTH 0.5 kW and 1.2 kW device powers. This is flagged as an extreme-conservatism limitation. The synthetic decision matrix alone cannot validate k selection; the per-model coverage/utilization trade-off is the primary basis. Real-world validation on co-located data (ESP32, Phase 8) is required to assess actual ALLOW/DENY behavior.
limitations: The synthetic decision evaluation is based on only 176 synthetically aligned solar/load pairs. It demonstrates the decision logic but is NOT evidence of zero real-world grid-usage violations.
Sigma estimation and coverage evaluation use the same held-out backtest residuals; coverage is NOT an independent out-of-sample calibration result.
The chosen k should be validated on real co-located data (ESP32, Phase 8) before deployment.
sigma_method_for_deployed_decision_engin: bucketed (solar: cloud-cover bucket, load: hour-of-day block)
sigma_method_for_synthetic_matrix: both bucketed and global reported separately
